summary: The article surveys local initiatives aimed at closing the gender gap in STEM, from middle school coding workshops and scholarships to mentorship, bootcamps, shared workspaces, outreach partnerships, and networking events. Most programs launched in September to November 2023 and are led by local developers, entrepreneurs, and educators. The piece concludes that grassroots momentum is growing, though true gender parity has not yet been reached.
one_line: Local programs launched in fall 2023, including coding workshops, scholarships, mentoring, and networking, are working to increase women's participation in STEM and tech.
key_facts: Techie Girls launched on September 15, 2023 at Morton Middle School, led by software developer Emily Chan, and offers weekly coding workshops for girls in grades 6 through 8.
Future Femme Tech has awarded 30 scholarships since its inception on October 3, 2023, to women entering STEM disciplines at the local university.
MentorHer Tech was launched on November 12, 2023 by tech entrepreneur Maya Jackson and pairs experienced tech professionals with women starting or transitioning into tech careers.
Mentee Sofia Gonzalez credits MentorHer Tech with her swift adaptation to the tech industry.

The Code Queen Initiative, started in early September 2023 by front-end developer Li Jing, hosts workshops ranging from app development to cybersecurity and accommodates hurdles such as childcare responsibilities.
HerTech Hub, founded by a coalition of female tech leaders, opened on September 22, 2023 and offers a shared workspace, resources, and networking opportunities for women in tech.
Georgia Liu says spaces like HerTech Hub banish the 'impostor syndrome' many women feel in male-dominated workspaces.
InfinitiTech has partnered with Women in STEM Alliance on the STEM Outreach Program, which reaches girls in underserved communities through tech fairs, science camps, and school visits.
Outreach director Keith Morrison says that for many girls the program is their first encounter with the world of tech.
ConnectHer, a networking event launched on September 30, 2023, brings together women from various tech disciplines to share knowledge, experiences, and opportunities.
Dr. Lauren Murphy recently received the 'Tech Innovator of the Year' award for her work in sustainable energy solutions.
Angela Richardson, a venture catalyst, argues that funding and supporting women-led tech ventures is essential for diverse innovation.
Educator Vanessa Torres says encouragement of women into tech must start when girls are young rather than waiting until college.
